cross_references.note: CA_Labor_Employment_Litigator owns the employment discrimination and retaliation track under §12940. This standard owns the disability accommodation and interactive process layer. Both Citizens analyze §12940 from different angles; coordinate to avoid double-counting but ensure both tracks are pled.

Workers compensation (WCAB track) and FEHA accommodation (civil court track) run simultaneously. The industrial injury that grounds the WC claim is the same disability triggering FEHA §12940(m)/(n). WCAB exclusive jurisdiction does not preempt the FEHA disability discrimination claim.

ADA Title I (42 USC §12112) is the federal parallel to FEHA §12940 disability accommodation. A violation of ADA Title I is also a violation of FEHA under §12926(n) (broader ADA coverage incorporated). Both tracks can be pursued simultaneously through coordinated CRD/EEOC filing.
GOV §12965 governs the CRD complaint filing, right-to-sue issuance, and civil action SOL. Administrative exhaustion under §12965 is the prerequisite for civil suit on §12940(m)/(n) claims.

Where the disability discrimination occurs in a business establishment context (not just employment), Unruh Civil Rights Act (CIV §51) runs parallel to FEHA §12940. Unruh does not require CRD exhaustion — direct civil action with $4,000 minimum statutory damages per offense.
